Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
638 AM EDT Sun Sep 6 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 233 AM EDT Sunday...

No significant changes have been made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 233 AM EDT Sunday...

1. Mostly dry weather will continue through Tuesday.

2. Widespread rain expected Wednesday night and Thursday 
morning. Mostly dry conditions expected late week into next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 233 AM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: A few rain showers continue across the region this hour, 
but will gradually diminish through the morning. Although an 
isolated shower or two may be possible today, especially across the 
high terrain, dry weather is expected to prevail. Temperatures today 
will be on the cooler side, generally in the upper 60s to low 70s. 
Clearing skies will allow for efficient radiational cooling tonight, 
with lows falling into the 40s and 50s, with some of the colder 
hollows dropping into the upper 30s. A brief period of ridging looks 
to build in for Monday, continuing to bring mostly dry conditions 
throughout the day. A weak cold front pushing through Monday night 
may bring spark some light rain showers, particularly near the 
Canadian border.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A rather vigorous shortwave trough will be speeding 
through the longwave pattern Wednesday night and Thursday. This 
feature is expected to entrain an impressive plume of moisture from 
the Gulf with PWAT values surging to 2+ inches (2-3 standard 
deviations above normal). This will allow a period of moderate to 
heavy rainfall to move across the region during the overnight hours. 
However, moist adiabatic lapse profiles up to 200 mb leave much to be 
desired in terms of instability which should inhibit any 
thunderstorms potential, Thus, we expect more of a beneficial 
rainfall event with the hydrological issue appear unlikely at this 
time. A strong 100+ knot 500 mb jet and 30-45 kt LLJ will help to 
quickly push this system to our east with most of the rainfall 
exiting the region by daybreak on Thursday. 

A broad upper level trough will remain across the region Thursday 
and Friday which could set the stage for some isolated to scattered 
afternoon showers but additional rainfall will be light as the deep 
plume of moisture will be shunted eastward. Global deterministic and 
ensemble guidance are coming into better agreement in showing that 
mid-level height rises appear likely late Friday into next weekend 
which should bring drier conditions back to the region.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 12Z Monday...Widely variable conditions exist across the
region this morning. Low stratus is bringing MVFR to IFR 
ceilings to many places while VFR conditions are being observed 
outside of the low stratus. We should see this stratus mix
through the morning hours with improvement to VFR conditions at
all terminals by 14Z. Winds will be out of the north today with
some gusty winds up to 20 knots across the Champlain Valley and
KEFK. Winds will go light and variable overnight with fog likely
in the sheltered river valleys. We are already hinting at fog at
KEFK, KSLK, and KMPV as models seem to be in good agreement with
fog developing after 7Z.

Outlook...

Labor Day: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. Likely SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Definite
SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
